seo.title: Strategy Pattern: Keep change where it belongs
seo.description: Learn the Strategy pattern through an interactive payment example. See the problem, structural change, benefits, tradeoffs, and a TypeScript implementation.
seo.ogDescription: Watch a growing conditional become a set of interchangeable payment strategies.
seo.headline: Strategy pattern: keep change where it belongs
seo.articleDescription: Learn the Strategy pattern through an interactive payment example.

lesson.request: One checkout flow, different payment methods
lesson.scenario: Checkout already supports card and wallet payments. Now it needs points payments. Each method completes a payment, but charging, balance validation, and points calculation follow different rules. Where should the new rules live so the checkout flow does not need repeated edits?
lesson.principleTitle: Encapsulate payment rules as interchangeable strategies
lesson.problem: A conditional is not inherently wrong. The problem is that every new payment method adds another branch to Checkout, making a stable workflow responsible for more rule details.
lesson.solution: Define a shared payment strategy interface and put card, wallet, and points rules in separate implementations. Checkout only invokes payment behavior; the caller supplies the strategy selected by the user.
keyIdeas: Checkout decides when to pay; a concrete strategy decides how to pay.
Strategies follow the same interface and are interchangeable from the caller's perspective.
A new points strategy works through the existing checkout interface.
benefits: Adding a payment method mainly extends a separate strategy instead of adding payment branches to Checkout.
Each set of payment rules can be implemented and tested independently, making failures easier to locate.
User choices or business conditions can select a different payment strategy at runtime.
lesson.tradeoff: The design adds an interface, implementations, and strategy selection code. The caller must still understand when each strategy is appropriate, and registration and selection logic still need maintenance. The pattern does not eliminate every kind of change.
lesson.when: A task has interchangeable algorithms or rules that evolve independently, such as payment, shipping calculations, discounts, or sorting. Callers need to switch rules without depending on implementation details.
lesson.avoid: There are only one or two stable approaches, no replacement is needed, and more rules are unlikely. A direct function or conditional is often clearer.
lesson.remember: One checkout, different payment strategies. The stable flow decides when to pay; the interchangeable strategy decides how.
lesson.distinction: Strategy lets the caller select alternative algorithms for one task. State focuses on an object's current state and transitions. Template Method fixes the sequence of an algorithm while letting subclasses replace individual steps.

stages.label: The original
stages.title: The checkout owns every decision
stages.description: Checkout handles the order and knows the details of each payment method.
stages.insight: One module now changes for two reasons: the checkout flow and payment rules.
stages.graphNote: Checkout knows each payment method and makes the choice itself.
stages.codeNote: See how checkout selects card or wallet.

stages.label: A new request
stages.title: Add points as a payment method
stages.description: A small new option means opening Checkout again and extending its branch logic.
stages.insight: Every new method forces a change inside otherwise stable checkout code.
stages.graphNote: Points is new, but the conditional inside checkout must change too.
stages.codeNote: A new points branch changes the checkout function.

stages.label: Extract a strategy
stages.title: Put variation behind one interface
stages.description: Checkout depends on a payment behavior. Card and wallet payments implement it separately.
stages.insight: The main flow asks for payment without knowing how that payment works.
stages.graphNote: Move payment rules behind an interface. Checkout only calls pay.
stages.codeNote: Replace conditionals with an interface and separate strategies.

stages.label: Extend again
stages.title: Add an implementation, keep the flow
stages.description: Points payment joins as another strategy. Checkout needs no new branch.
stages.insight: The change stays in a new strategy. The tradeoff is one more abstraction.
stages.graphNote: Add the points strategy. Checkout and existing strategies stay unchanged.
stages.codeNote: Add PointsPayment. The checkout function is unchanged.
